metadata.dominant_domain_inferred: long-form personal-finance, money-psychology, real-estate, auction-acquisition and anti-gambling essays for a Brazilian audience
metadata.core_promise_of_system: Make abstract money topics feel urgent, personal, morally loaded and immediately actionable by translating the Brazilian macroeconomy into high-stakes life consequences, exposing betting traps and misunderstood auction mechanics.
metadata.primary_content_engine: History/metaphor-driven warning essay that reframes a familiar financial idea as misunderstood, structurally rigged, psychologically dangerous, and still navigable if the viewer adopts the creator's framework.
metadata.character_length_rule: The final FULL SCRIPT must be no less than 7,000 characters and no more than 9,000 characters.

audience_inference.psychological_state: skeptical, economically uneasy, wants clarity and edge, feels mainstream advice (banks, managers, media, simplified guidance) is incomplete or too late, distrusts easy-money promises via bets or miracle auctions
audience_inference.aspirational_identity: calm, informed, anti-hype, anti-betting, system-level thinker who spots traps before the crowd — someone who understands the Brazilian game beyond 'save in poupança and buy a house through Caixa'

authority_basis: claims personal investing experience in Brazil

references long study time and obscure documents (Central Bank regulations, CVM, SUSEP, PREVIC, Receita Federal, IBGE, IPEA, Tesouro Nacional, B3, Caixa Econômica Federal, Detran, court auctions, auction edicts, Law 14.790/2023 on betting, Law 9.514/1997 on fiduciary alienation, Law 8.245/1991 on leases, Civil Code, CDC, City Statute)
uses Brazilian and global historical analogies
frames advice as mechanical, not motivational
signals distance from schemes, courses, hype, bets and easy-money promises
mentions hands-on experience with Receita Federal, Central Bank, CVM, B3, Caixa, Detran, official auctioneers, and the Brazilian mortgage market

cross_sample_system.dominant_pattern: Each video opens with a striking anecdote or historical event, converts it into a present-day parallel, exposes a hidden structural trap (financial, real-estate, auction or betting), escalates consequences from portfolio-level to life-level, then resolves with a practical protocol and a worldview shift.
what_is_repeated_across_samples: Title promises revelation plus correction of a false belief.
Cold open uses a vivid story, person or date cluster before the thesis.
Immediate pivot: 'this is happening again / right now / to you.'
Presenter positions himself as an obsessive researcher, not an entertainer.
Viewer is told mainstream advice is directionally true but dangerously incomplete.
Concepts are reduced to one central metaphor carried across the script.
Repeated contrast between spreadsheet math and human psychology.
Frequent use of named characters or mini-case studies to concretise abstractions.
Action steps appear after fear/diagnosis, never before.
Endings compress the message into 3 takeaways or a concise doctrine.
Auctions are presented as a serious tool, not a lottery.
Bets are presented as a mathematical and psychological trap, never as income.
what_is_intentionally_avoided: No dry textbook exposition without emotional framing.
No jargon left untranslated for long.
No absolute certainty; uses probabilistic seriousness.
No purely technical CTA; CTAs are embedded as practical tools, not hard sells.
No celebratory finance-bro energy, no luxury signalling, no macho alpha posture.
No references to exclusively American institutions or products (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, Fannie Mae) without translation to Brazilian equivalents.
No glorification of betting, bets, tigrinho, online casinos or gambling.
No promise of fast enrichment via auctions.
exceptions_used_strategically: Video 4 is simpler and more direct; less nuanced than the others because it targets urgency and beginner conversion.
Video 6 leans more speculative/conspiratorial but protects credibility with repeated disclaimers about lack of proof.
Video 7 is more constructive and motivational, but still framed through pain, misperception and psychological failure.
Video 8 focuses exclusively on the Brazilian property market and the traps of financing, Minha Casa Minha Vida, consórcio and property auctions.
Video 9 focuses exclusively on vehicle auctions (Detran, Caixa, judicial, extrajudicial) and the traps of documentation, total loss, recovery and resale.
Video 10 focuses exclusively on fighting betting: Bets, tigrinho, Fortune Tiger, Blaze, Betano, Sportingbet, jogo do bicho, online casinos, and how to exit addiction.

rotation_mandate.purpose: Force thematic diversity across videos. Prevent the model from collapsing into real-estate, auctions or anti-betting on every generation. The blueprint's terminology and sample set are heavily skewed toward property, auctions and betting; without an explicit rotation rule, the model defaults to those categories because they satisfy the content formula most easily and provide the strongest emotional hooks.
rotation_mandate.principle: Every generated script must be assigned to ONE category. Categories rotate. Consecutive videos must never share the same category. Real-estate, auctions and anti-betting have hard caps, but anti-betting is treated as a public-service category with a higher frequency allowance because it addresses a public-health epidemic.

selection_rules: Track the last six videos produced by the channel and their assigned categories.
Before generating a new script, choose the category that has been used LEAST recently. On a tie, prefer the category with fewer appearances in the last twelve videos.
Never generate two consecutive videos in the same category.
The real_estate_financing and asset_auctions categories each have a hard cap: at most one in every four videos.
The anti_gambling category has a higher cap: at most one in every three videos, and never consecutively.
If the channel has no history (first video), default to one of: money_psychology, concentration_indexing, or macro_currency.
If the user has explicitly requested a topic, honour it, but flag the rule violation in a single sentence inside the script's internal notes (not in the script body).
rotation_mandate.user_command_override: The user's explicit topic request always wins, but the generation model must warn in one sentence if the request breaks the rotation rule (e.g., 'this will be your third real-estate video in a row').
anti_patterns_to_avoid: Do not default to real estate, auctions or anti-betting as the 'most compelling' or 'most urgent' category.

Do not use property, auction or casino metaphors as the central metaphor for non-property, non-auction or non-betting categories. Use different physical metaphors instead: gansos, banheira, bola de neve, banco de três pernas, ponte, engrenagens, jardim, jarro, portão, poço, fogo, semente, tear, escada, mapa, bússola, rio, represa, âncora, muro, castelo, navio, motor, roda, espelho, eco, sombra, fio, corrente, farol, túnel, escada, rede, peneira, esponja, prisma, polia, válvula, fechadura, balança, carrinho de mão, mochila, reservatório.
Do not reference mortgage rates, property taxes, ITBI or housing markets as primary evidence in non-property categories.
Do not reference auction edicts, leiloeiro comissões or vehicle salvage as primary evidence in non-auction categories.
Do not reference betting odds, tigrinho mechanics or casino psychology as primary evidence in non-betting categories.

Do not use the viewer's own home as the emotional anchor in non-property categories. Anchor instead to their salary, their FGTS balance, their savings, their time, their family, their career, or their future retirement.
Do not use the viewer's own car as the emotional anchor in non-auction categories.

macro_flow: 1. Pattern interrupt opening: bizarre anecdote, historical collapse or jarring scenario with Brazilian relevance (1980s-90s hyperinflation, Plano Real, 1999 crisis, 2008 crisis, 2015-2016 crisis, COVID, 2022 inflation, betting scandal, Americanas crisis, tigrinho case, miraculous property auctions).
2. Snap-link to present relevance: 'the same pattern is happening now.'
3. Presenter framing: why he is qualified / why this isn't hype.
4. Promise stack: explicit list of what the viewer will understand by the end.
5. Tool CTA early: free calculator/report framed as corrective utility.
7. Conceptual explanation with simple language and arithmetic.
9. Psychological complication: why humans fail even when the math works.
10. Concrete examples/case studies with named people and specific numbers in BRL.
12. Identity-level conclusion: freedom comes from mindset/system, not mere returns.
13. Final compression into takeaways + soft internal CTA to another video/subscribe.

opening_pattern.method: Start with a highly specific anecdote before the thesis so the viewer is mentally hooked by narrative, not argument.
opening_pattern.why_it_works: The viewer unconsciously asks 'why are you telling me this?' and the script answers by connecting the anecdote to their money/life.
opening_variants: Brazilian historical scam/collapse (hyperinflation, 1990 poupança confiscation, Plano Real, 1999 crisis, 2008 crisis, 2015-2016 crisis, Americanas, bets, tigrinho)
ordinary person scenario with hidden flaw
IBGE or Central Bank data used as a shock
real auction gone wrong (hidden debt, occupation, salvage vehicle)
real betting case that destroyed a family

pacing_model.rhythm: Dense but segmented. Short-to-medium sentences dominate, broken by longer explanatory runs after hooks land.
pacing_model.acceleration_pattern: Hook -> explanation -> new danger -> deeper mechanism -> practical release.
retention_devices: forward promises ('here's what we're doing today')
counterintuitive turns ('the math works, human psychology doesn't')
alternation between macro and personal examples
references to familiar Brazilian institutions (Central Bank, Receita Federal, CVM, IBGE, B3, Caixa, Detran)

beliefs: Most financial pain comes from incentives and psychology, not lack of information alone.
Institutions optimise for system preservation, not your well-being.
Conventional advice is often half-true and dangerous when decontextualised.
Freedom is more about flexibility, margin and enoughness than maximising returns.
The disciplined ordinary person can outperform the emotional crowd.
The Brazilian system has specific vulnerabilities that most mainstream advice ignores.
Understanding the interplay between Receita Federal, Central Bank, CVM and the mortgage market is essential for financial safety in Brazil.
Poupança is not an investment; it is an emergency reserve with negative real return.
Depending exclusively on INSS is a systemic risk for most Brazilians.
Brazilian taxation is complex by design; ignorance is expensive.
Consórcio is not an investment; it is a programmed purchase with fees.
Auctions are not a lottery; they are a serious tool with real risks.
Bets, tigrinho, Fortune Tiger, Blaze, Betano, Sportingbet are not investments; they are games of chance with negative mathematical expectation.
Betting addiction is a disease; there is treatment and an exit.
The culture of 'easy money' is a trap.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.status_framing: High status is attached to calm realism, delayed gratification and structural understanding, not flashy consumption.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.fear_framing: The real danger is not one crash or one bad pick; it is building your life on false assumptions — especially about property, retirement, auctions and betting.
worldview_embedded_in_scripts.transformation_promise: Move from reactive participant to system-aware allocator who can't be easily trapped — someone who understands the Brazilian rules better than the average Brazilian, including auctions and betting.

content_formula.step_1: Choose a financial topic with mainstream familiarity and hidden complexity, WITHIN the category assigned by the rotation_mandate (poupança, CDB, Tesouro Direto, PGBL, VGBL, Minha Casa Minha Vida, FGTS, consórcio, property auctions, vehicle auctions, Bets, tigrinho).
content_formula.step_2: Find a Brazilian historical analogy, strange anecdote or sharp mini-story that mirrors the modern issue.
content_formula.step_3: Frame the common understanding as incomplete or dangerously naive.
content_formula.step_4: Introduce one sticky metaphor that can carry the full explanation. Prefer non-property, non-auction and non-betting metaphors unless the assigned category is one of those.
content_formula.step_5: Translate the mechanism into plain arithmetic with concrete BRL numbers.
content_formula.step_6: Add a human-failure layer: why people still mess this up even when the math is knowable.
content_formula.step_7: Insert one or more case studies with names, ages, incomes, balances, outcomes.
content_formula.step_8: Escalate from portfolio consequence to lifestyle, identity or societal consequence.
content_formula.step_9: Offer a protocol/ruleset that feels practical, not magical.
content_formula.step_10: End with worldview compression and a concise memorable doctrine.

stylistic_rules_for_future_outputs: Never explain a concept without an image/object/metaphor.
Use numbers to anchor trust, not to overwhelm.
Alternate macro systems and individual stories.
Speak as if correcting a dangerous misunderstanding.
Let skepticism and humility coexist: strong thesis, selective uncertainty.
Avoid sounding like a trader; sound like a strategic realist.
Give the viewer dignity through understanding, not through hype.
Use Brazilian-specific references (Receita Federal, Central Bank, CVM, IBGE, budget, Tesouro Direto, CDB, LCI, PGBL, VGBL, Minha Casa Minha Vida, FGTS, auctions, Bets).
Avoid American financial terms (401k, Roth IRA, Social Security, 30-year fixed, FICO score, etc.) without translation.
Never glorify betting; always expose the math and the psychology of addiction.
Never promise fast enrichment via auctions; always expose risks and protocols.
Treat auctions as a serious tool, not as a lottery.
Treat betting victims with compassion, not contempt.
title_generation_rules: Centre danger, reversal or hidden mechanism.
Use direct second-order implications: not just 'recession' but 'worse than the 2008 crisis.'
Make titles feel like practical protection against a trap.
Include Brazilian specificity whenever possible ('your poupança', 'your FGTS', 'Receita Federal', 'B3', 'Minha Casa Minha Vida', 'Detran', 'Bets').
hook_generation_rules: Open on a vivid story or date cluster before introducing the topic.
Reveal the present-day relevance within the first 5–8 lines.
Promise a deeper mechanism, not just surface explanation.
